To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a hierarchical organization of a face database using metric learning with LBP features can lead to a more accurate system than a flat organization; 2) the hierarchical organization also leads to a more efficient system, with a significant speed up for retrieval; 3) the hierarchical organization is also more robust to noise in the data, i.e. the system is able to handle a larger number of distracting faces without compromising the performance.

(1) the proposed method outperforms all state of the art methods on LFW; (2) the proposed method is significantly faster than all the existing state of the art systems; and (3) the proposed method can be easily applied to large-scale face databases, such as the one with millions of faces used in this study, and can be extended to other face retrieval problems.

(i) LBP features are highly resilient to appearance variations and are efficient to calculate; (ii) metric learning approaches have shown to be successful for face verification in the wild; (iii) organizing the database hierarcically with local metric learning leads to more accurate and efficient identity-based face search.
